title: SAML 2.0 Basics
description: Learn SAML 2.0 protocol fundamentals, assertions, bindings, and how to integrate enterprise identity providers.

data.text: **SAML 2.0** (Security Assertion Markup Language) is an XML-based open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between parties. It remains the dominant protocol for enterprise Single Sign-On, especially in organizations using Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) or other on-premises identity infrastructure.

data.caption: SAML 2.0 Web Browser SSO flow using HTTP Redirect and POST bindings.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant SP as Service Provider
    participant IdP as Identity Provider
    U->>SP: Access protected resource
    SP->>SP: Generate AuthnRequest
    SP->>U: Redirect to IdP with SAMLRequest
    U->>IdP: POST AuthnRequest
    IdP->>IdP: Authenticate user
    IdP->>U: POST SAML Response (Assertion)
    U->>SP: Forward SAML Response
    SP->>SP: Validate signature & assertion
    SP->>U: Grant access with session

data.title: Core Components
items: **AuthnRequest**: SP request asking the IdP to authenticate a user.
**Assertion Consumer Service (ACS)**: SP endpoint that receives and processes SAML responses.
**SAML Assertion**: XML document containing user identity, authentication time, and attributes.
**Identity Provider Entity ID**: Unique URI identifying the IdP.
**Service Provider Entity ID**: Unique URI identifying your application.

data.title: Assertions, Not Tokens
data.text: SAML uses "assertions" — cryptographically signed XML documents. Unlike JWTs, SAML assertions are typically larger, verbose, and validated against an X.509 certificate.

rows: Base64-encoded request in URL query string

data.title: Simplified SAML Assertion
data.content: A SAML Response contains an encrypted or signed Assertion with user identity and attributes.
data.code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<saml2p:Response 
    xmlns:saml2p="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol"
    ID="_response_id" 
    Version="2.0" 
    IssueInstant="2026-01-15T10:00:00Z"
    Destination="https://app.example.com/saml/acs"
    Consent="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:consent:unspecified">
  
  <saml2:Issuer xmlns:saml2="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">
    https://idp.example.com
  </saml2:Issuer>
  
  <saml2p:Status>
    <saml2p:StatusCode Value="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Success"/>
  </saml2p:Status>
  
  <saml2:Assertion 
      xmlns:saml2="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"
      ID="_assertion_id" 
      IssueInstant="2026-01-15T10:00:05Z" 
      Version="2.0">
    
    <saml2:Issuer>https://idp.example.com</saml2:Issuer>
    <saml2:Subject>
      <saml2:NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress">
        user@example.com
      </saml2:NameID>
      <saml2:SubjectConfirmation Method="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer">
        <saml2:SubjectConfirmationData 
            NotOnOrAfter="2026-01-15T10:05:00Z" 
            Recipient="https://app.example.com/saml/acs"/>
      </saml2:SubjectConfirmation>
    </saml2:Subject>
    
    <saml2:Conditions 
        NotBefore="2026-01-15T09:55:00Z" 
        NotOnOrAfter="2026-01-15T10:05:00Z">
      <saml2:AudienceRestriction>
        <saml2:Audience>https://app.example.com</saml2:Audience>
      </saml2:AudienceRestriction>
    </saml2:Conditions>
    
    <saml2:AuthnStatement 
        AuthnInstant="2026-01-15T10:00:05Z" 
        SessionIndex="_session_123">
      <saml2:AuthnContext>
        <saml2:AuthnContextClassRef>
          urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport
        </saml2:AuthnContextClassRef>
      </saml2:AuthnContext>
    </saml2:AuthnStatement>
  </saml2:Assertion>
</saml2p:Response>

data.title: Configuring SAML authentication in ASP.NET Core
data.content: Use a library like Sustainsys.Saml2 to handle SAML 2.0 in ASP.NET Core.

data.title: Certificate Management
data.text: SAML relies heavily on X.509 certificates for signing and encryption. Store certificates securely (use Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager), rotate them before expiry, and never commit private keys to source control.

data.title: What Goes Wrong
items: Clock skew: SAML assertions have strict time windows. Ensure IdP and SP servers are NTP-synchronized.
Entity ID mismatch: The AudienceRestriction must exactly match the SP EntityID.
Certificate mismatches: The signing certificate used by the IdP must be trusted by the SP.
POST binding issues: Ensure your ACS endpoint accepts POST requests and is not blocked by CSRF tokens.
Attribute mapping: Map SAML attributes to the correct claim types in your identity system.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SAML 2.0 is XML-based and dominant in enterprise SSO
AuthnRequest and Assertion are the two primary message types
Assertions contain user identity, authentication time, and attributes
Certificates are central to SAML trust and must be managed carefully
SAML is verbose but battle-tested; OIDC is preferred for new apps
data.takeaway: SAML 2.0 remains the enterprise standard for SSO, but its complexity requires careful configuration and certificate management.
